newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher on back of Siderca.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher on back of Siderca.

text.p: Argentine stocks recouped early losses and closed higher Thursday, boosted by stronger-than-expected half-year profits for steelmaker Siderca, dealers said.
"Siderca's results beat even the most optimistic forecasts and pulled the market out of negative territory," said Humberto Lopez at Wainbuch traders.

The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 0.6 percent to 583.29, virtually erasing losses incurred Wednesday when local players feared a wave of profit-taking after a bull run on Wall Street capping the U.S. presidential elections.
"Siderca's results to a certain degree reflect the pace of economic recovery, mainly in the export sector, which cheered many players," said a trader at a U.S.-based bank.
Siderca posted a net six-month profit of $86.9 million compared to $9.1 million in the same period of 1995.
"But if Wall Street had slumped today, we would probably have done the same. You have to take this rise with a pinch of salt -- we've not yet consolidated recent gains," he added.
The MerVal rose 4.3 percent between October 28-November 5.
The broad market edged up 0.2 percent Thursday, with risers beating decliners 27 to 18 and 19 issues closed flat.

Floor volume rose to 21.4 million pesos from 18.8 million Wednesday, although it included a 6.4 million block trade for biscuit maker Bagley, a second-tier stock which closed unchanged. Over-the-counter deals rose to 88.4 million pesos from 76.9 million Wednesday.

Top main-tier gainers were Siderca, carmaker Sevel and construction stock Polledo, which rose 4.6 percent, 4.3 percent and 2.1 percent, respectively. Worst MerVal performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa and real estate developer Irsa, off 2.3 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
